title: Transverse coding preserves obliviousness
statement: Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, let $e$ embed the Booleans into $A$, and let $P$ be a finite Turing machine over $A$. If, on any two inputs of equal length and at every time $t\in\mathbb N$, $P$ has the same input-head position and the same work-tape head positions, then its transverse binary realization has this same property on every pair of equal-length binary inputs, at every time.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ is finite and has decidable equality
$P$ is a finite Turing machine over $A$
$P$ has equal head positions at every time on any two equal-length inputs
replaced:
Let $P$ be a machine over a finite alphabet $A$ and $e$ an embedding of the Booleans
into $A$. If $P$ is oblivious, then the transverse binary realization of $P$ is
oblivious — at all intermediate physical times and at all times after halting.
